The '''2022 Plymouth City Council election''' took place on 5 May 2022 to elect members of [[Plymouth City Council]] in England. It coincided with [[2022 United Kingdom local elections|local elections across the United Kingdom]]. The Conservative Party made gains in the previous election in 2021, resulting in the council entering [[no overall control]] with no party holding a majority of seats. Immediately following the results of the 2022 election, the council remained in no overall control. Labour and the Conservatives gained seats from independent councillors who had left their parties and exchanged seats with each other. The election saw the elections of the city's first [[Green Party of England and Wales|Green Party]] councillor, Ian Poyser, and first [[Transgender|trans]] councillor, [[Dylan Tippetts]] of the Labour Party.

Shortly after the election, five councillors who had resigned from the Conservative group under the previous council leader Nick Kelly returned to their party, giving the Conservatives an overall majority. The independent councillor George Wheeler, who had originally been elected as a Labour councillor, joined the Green Party.

== Background ==

=== History ===
[[File:Plymouth City Council election 2018 map.svg|thumb|Result of the council election when these seats were last contested in 2018]]
[[File:Plymouth City Council election 2021 map.svg|thumb|Result of the most recent council election in 2021]]
Plymouth City Council held local elections as part of the [[2022 United Kingdom local elections|2022 local elections]]. The council elects its councillors in thirds, with a third of seats being up for election every year for three years, and no election each fourth year, to correspond with councillors' four-year terms.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.gov.uk/guidance/local-government-structure-and-elections#electoral-cycles|title=Local government structure and elections|work=GOV.UK|access-date=2018-04-27|language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://assets.publishing.service.gov.uk/government/uploads/system/uploads/attachment_data/file/694598/Election_Timetable_in_England.pdf|title=Election Timetable in England}}</ref> Councillors defending their seats in this election were previously elected in [[2018 Plymouth City Council election|2018]]. In that election, eleven Labour candidates and eight Conservative candidates were elected.

Elections in Plymouth are usually competitive between the Labour Party and the Conservative Party.<ref>{{Cite news |date=2022-04-12 |title=Third of Devon's city councils seats up for election |language=en-GB |work=BBC News |url=https://www.bbc.com/news/uk-england-devon-61066897 |access-date=2022-04-12}}</ref> The council was controlled by the Labour Party from the [[2018 Plymouth City Council election]] until the [[2021 Plymouth City Council election]], when the council entered [[no overall control]], with no party holding a majority of seats. One Labour councillor elected in 2018—Kevin Neil—was suspended from his party in the same year.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Eve |first=Carl |date=2018-09-25 |title=Police investigation into suspended Labour councillor dropped |url=https://www.plymouthherald.co.uk/news/plymouth-news/police-investigation-plymouth-labour-councillor-2041534 |access-date=2022-03-23 |website=PlymouthLive |language=en}}</ref> Another Labour councillor, Chaz Singh, left his party in 2019.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Eve |first=Carl |date=2019-09-27 |title=The real reason Chaz Singh quit the Labour Party |url=https://www.plymouthherald.co.uk/news/plymouth-news/real-reason-plymouth-councillor-chaz-3354994 |access-date=2022-03-23 |website=PlymouthLive |language=en}}</ref> Several Conservative councillors left their group to sit as independents, including the former council leader Ian Bowyer, after two of them were suspended by the group leader Nick Kelly for publishing a press release supporting a reduction in the speed limit on the A38 road through the city.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Oldfield |first=Edward |date=2020-10-09 |title=Senior councillors quit Tory group and criticise leadership |url=https://www.plymouthherald.co.uk/news/plymouth-news/senior-plymouth-tories-quit-council-4590909 |access-date=2022-03-23 |website=PlymouthLive |language=en}}</ref>

=== Developments since 2021 ===
The Conservatives made gains in the [[2021 Plymouth City Council election]] and Nick Kelly was voted in as council leader with a minority of seats.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Green |first=Alex |date=2021-06-09 |title=Meet the man who's now in charge of Plymouth |url=https://www.plymouthherald.co.uk/news/plymouth-news/meet-nick-kelly-born-bred-5504257 |access-date=2022-03-23 |website=PlymouthLive |language=en}}</ref> In October 2021, the Conservative councillor Shannon Burden left the Conservative group to sit as an independent.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Eve |first=Carl |date=2021-10-06 |title=Plymouth Conservatives lose another councillor |url=https://www.plymouthherald.co.uk/news/plymouth-news/plymouth-conservatives-lose-another-councillor-6011068 |access-date=2022-03-23 |website=PlymouthLive |language=en}}</ref> In November 2021, the Conservative councillor Nigel Churchill left his party to sit as an independent councillor after he said complaints about breaches of the code of conduct were not being properly investigated.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Eve |first=Carl |date=2021-11-05 |title=Councillor quits Tory party over 'unacceptable' conduct |url=https://www.plymouthherald.co.uk/news/plymouth-news/councillor-quits-tory-party-alleging-6153594 |access-date=2022-03-23 |website=PlymouthLive |language=en}}</ref> In the same month, Kelly was suspended from the Conservative Party over an interview about the murder of Bobbi-Anne McLeod in which he had said "everybody has a responsibility not to try to put themselves in a compromising position", which was characterised as [[victim blaming]] by women politicians in the city.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Eve |first=Carl |date=2021-11-30 |title=Council leader suspended over Bobbi-Anne comments |url=https://www.plymouthherald.co.uk/news/plymouth-news/bobbi-anne-comments-lead-plymouth-6282792 |access-date=2022-03-23 |website=PlymouthLive |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=2021-11-30 |title=Tories suspend Plymouth council leader after 'victim-blaming' remarks |url=https://www.theguardian.com/society/2021/nov/30/tories-suspend-plymouth-council-leader-after-victim-blaming-remarks |access-date=2022-03-29 |website=The Guardian |language=en}}</ref> In January 2022, another Conservative councillor, Stephen Hulme, left the Conservative group to sit as an independent.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Eve |first=Carl |date=2022-01-10 |title=Plymouth Conservatives lose another councillor to Independents |url=https://www.plymouthherald.co.uk/news/plymouth-news/plymouth-conservatives-lose-yet-another-6470746 |access-date=2022-03-23 |website=PlymouthLive |language=en}}</ref> Kelly's suspension was lifted in the same month.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Eve |first=Carl |date=2022-01-10 |title=Tory leader's party suspension lifted |url=https://www.plymouthherald.co.uk/news/plymouth-news/plymouth-tory-leader-nick-kellys-6471505 |access-date=2022-03-23 |website=PlymouthLive |language=en}}</ref> In February 2022, another Conservative councillor, David Downie, was suspended from the group, leading to the Conservatives and Labour each having the same number of seats on the council.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Eve |first=Carl |date=2022-02-23 |title=Tories lose another councillor in Plymouth |url=https://www.plymouthherald.co.uk/news/plymouth-news/conservatives-lose-another-councillor-plymouth-6700552 |access-date=2022-03-23 |website=PlymouthLive |language=en}}</ref>

Kelly's budget failed to pass in February, with a Labour amendment passing instead that froze council tax. Labour called a vote of no confidence in Kelly.<ref>{{Cite web |last1=Clark |first1=Daniel |last2=Churm |first2=Philip |date=2022-03-11 |title=Plymouth City Council leader facing vote of no confidence |url=https://www.plymouthherald.co.uk/news/plymouth-news/plymouth-city-council-leader-nick-6789146 |access-date=2022-03-23 |website=PlymouthLive |language=en}}</ref> A Conservative councillor told the ''Plymouth Herald'' that some group members might abstain in the vote.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Eve |first=Carl |date=2022-03-18 |title=Some Conservatives 'to abstain' in leader no confidence vote |url=https://www.plymouthherald.co.uk/news/plymouth-news/conservatives-could-abstain-council-leader-6821069 |access-date=2022-03-23 |website=PlymouthLive |language=en}}</ref> Kelly lost the vote, with 29 councillors voting no confidence, 23 voting confidence and one abstaining.<ref>{{Cite news |date=2022-03-21 |title=Plymouth council leader ousted after no-confidence vote |language=en-GB |work=BBC News |url=https://www.bbc.com/news/uk-england-devon-60823305 |access-date=2022-03-23}}</ref> Independent councillors were split, with Singh supporting Kelly in the debate.<ref name="Churm">{{Cite web |last=Churm |first=Philip |date=2022-03-21 |title=Plymouth council leader ousted after less than a year in charge |url=https://www.plymouthherald.co.uk/news/plymouth-news/how-nick-kelly-ousted-leader-6839730 |access-date=2022-03-23 |website=PlymouthLive |language=en}}</ref> Two Conservative candidates were nominated to replace him: Vivien Pengelly, a former council leader, and Richard Bingley. Bingley was elected council leader with 26 votes to Pengelly's 12, with the remaining councillors abstaining.<ref name="Churm"/> Bingley had previously been in the Labour Party and the [[UK Independence Party]].<ref>{{Cite web |last1=Eve |first1=Carl |last2=Timms |first2=Katie |date=2022-03-22 |title=Senior figures lose roles as Plymouth's new cabinet announced |url=https://www.plymouthherald.co.uk/news/plymouth-news/plymouth-city-council-leader-richard-6844747 |access-date=2022-03-23 |website=PlymouthLive |language=en}}</ref>

Later in March, the [[lord mayor]] of Plymouth, the Conservative councillor Terri Beer, resigned from the Conservative group and the Conservative Party to sit as an independent councillor in response to Bingley's election, calling his new cabinet "lacking in experience and ability" and that her party locally had "been run into the ground by unelected chairpersons not from South West Devon".<ref>{{Cite web |title=Plymouth Lord Mayor resigns from Conservative group |url=https://planetradio.co.uk/greatest-hits/plymouth/news/plymouth-lord-mayor-resigns-from-tory-group/ |access-date=2022-03-29 |website=Greatest Hits Radio (Plymouth) |language=en}}</ref> She accused the new leadership of bullying. Her resignation meant that the Labour group had more councillors than the Conservatives.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Eve |first=Carl |date=2022-03-23 |title=Plymouth councillor quits Conservatives amid 'bullying' claim |url=https://www.plymouthherald.co.uk/news/plymouth-news/plymouth-councillor-quits-conservatives-amid-6851595 |access-date=2022-03-29 |website=PlymouthLive |language=en}}</ref>

== Campaign ==
The Conservative councillor David Downie was blocked from seeking selection by his local party in early 2022. He was suspended from the Conservative Party after questioning the decision, and later resigned his party membership after Richard Bingley became council leader. He said that the new cabinet had too many new councillors and he was "very concerned for the city, for the lack of experience and knowledge". In March 2022, he announced that he would run in Budshead as an independent candidate.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Churm |first=Philip |date=2022-03-25 |title=Former Plymouth Conservative councillor to stand as independent |url=https://www.plymouthherald.co.uk/news/plymouth-news/former-plymouth-conservative-councillor-dave-6858508 |access-date=2022-03-29 |website=PlymouthLive |language=en}}</ref>

Plymouth Labour published their manifesto on 30 March 2022. They pledged to cancel plans to remove bus shelters, invest money in roads and pavements, build more homes and buy empty properties.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Simpson |first=Zhara |date=2022-03-30 |title=Plymouth Labour party out to stop bus shelter closures |url=https://www.plymouthherald.co.uk/news/plymouth-news/plymouth-local-elections-labour-manifesto-6879856 |access-date=2022-03-31 |website=PlymouthLive |language=en}}</ref>

In April, recordings were published of a conversation between Bingley and the independent candidate Danny Bamping that had taken place in February. Bingley was recorded saying the then council leader Nick Kelly was a "weak, two-faced git" who had "been caught crossing me big time", and predicting that he would shortly no longer be council leader. He compared the Conservative councillor Maddi Bridgman to [[Izzat Ibrahim al-Douri]], who served as vice president to [[Saddam Hussein]], and said that the independent councillor Chaz Singh, who had supported Kelly, "needs to quickly shift his alliance". Kelly said he was "disappointed, appalled, and shocked".<ref name=":0" /> Bridgeman said she was "devastated by the vitriolic attack", and called for Bingley to resign, as well as asking their Conservative Association to suspend his membership.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |last=Churm |first=Philip |date=2022-04-01 |title=Plymouth council leader facing questions over leaked phone calls |url=https://www.plymouthherald.co.uk/news/plymouth-news/leaked-recordings-plymouth-council-leaders-6892017 |access-date=2022-04-02 |website=PlymouthLive |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Eve |first=Carl |date=2022-04-04 |title=Deputy Mayor calls for new council leader to be suspended |url=https://www.plymouthherald.co.uk/news/plymouth-news/deputy-mayor-left-devastated-calls-6898520 |access-date=2022-04-04 |website=PlymouthLive |language=en}}</ref> Margaret Boadella, the Conservative Association chair, said that people upset at Bingley's remarks should "do what I did when Downie was ranting at me, shut up and grow up".<ref>{{Cite web |last=Churm |first=Philip |date=2022-04-05 |title=Senior Tory says 'shut up and grow up' after leader's comments |url=https://www.plymouthherald.co.uk/news/plymouth-news/shut-up-grow-up-says-6907399 |access-date=2022-04-06 |website=PlymouthLive |language=en}}</ref>

''[[Plymouth Live]]'' reported that Bingley had appeared in a YouTube video in June 2020 in which he said people shouldn't "worry too much about climate change in itself", that people should cycle less, and that the [[COVID-19 pandemic]] was a "mildly severe flu pandemic".<ref>{{Cite web |last=Churm |first=Philip |date=2022-04-12 |title=Council leader says we 'shouldn't worry about climate change' |url=https://www.plymouthherald.co.uk/news/plymouth-news/plymouth-city-council-leader-richard-6944353 |access-date=2022-04-13 |website=PlymouthLive |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=2022-04-14 |title=Tory councillor dismisses climate and says we can adapt to 'barren, sandy landscapes' |url=https://www.independent.co.uk/climate-change/news/tory-mp-richard-bingley-climate-denial-b2057070.html |access-date=2022-04-22 |website=The Independent |language=en}}</ref> In response to the report, he said that he had taken action against climate change since becoming council leader, and that his comments about COVID had been made early in the pandemic.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Churm |first=Philip |date=2022-04-13 |title=Council leader insists climate change is a concern |url=https://www.plymouthherald.co.uk/news/plymouth-news/plymouth-city-council-leader-insists-6947392 |access-date=2022-04-13 |website=PlymouthLive |language=en}}</ref> Six councillors who had left the Conservative group to sit as independents during Kelly's leadership defended Bingley, saying that he had been smeared by "a small collective of disgruntled councillors".<ref>{{Cite web |last=Eve |first=Carl |date=2022-04-22 |title=Councillors claim smear campaign against new leader |url=https://www.plymouthherald.co.uk/news/plymouth-news/councillors-claim-smear-campaign-against-6982723 |access-date=2022-05-02 |website=PlymouthLive |language=en}}</ref>

Statements of persons nominated were published on 6 April listing all validly nominated candidates. In order to control a majority of seats on the council, the Conservatives would need to win twelve of the nineteen seats up for election, and Labour would need to win sixteen.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Clark |first=Daniel |date=2022-04-06 |title=Full list of candidates for Plymouth Council local elections |url=https://www.plymouthherald.co.uk/news/plymouth-news/every-plymouth-city-council-candidate-6911266 |access-date=2022-04-06 |website=PlymouthLive |language=en}}</ref>

== Results ==
=== Overall ===

The results saw Labour and the Conservatives level on twenty-four seats each. Each party gained seats from independent councillors who were originally elected from their parties. Dave Downie, originally a Conservative, was the only independent councillor to contest his former seat, Budshead, where he was beaten by the Conservative candidate. The Conservatives gained Southway from Labour, while Labour gained Compton from the Conservatives for the first time ever.<ref name="Herald-results">{{Cite web |last1=Eve |first1=Carl |last2=Clark |first2=Daniel |date=2022-05-06 |title=Plymouth City Council remains under no overall control |url=https://www.plymouthherald.co.uk/news/plymouth-news/plymouth-city-council-remains-under-7044634 |access-date=2022-05-06 |website=PlymouthLive |language=en}}</ref> The [[Green Party of England and Wales|Green Party]] won their first ever seat on the council, with their candidate Ian Poyser gaining Plympton Chaddlewood from the Conservatives.<ref>{{Cite news |date=2022-05-06 |title=Plymouth election results 2022: City council under no overall control |language=en-GB |work=BBC News |url=https://www.bbc.com/news/uk-england-devon-61332633 |access-date=2022-05-06}}</ref> [[Dylan Tippetts]], the new Labour councillor for Compton, became the first [[Transgender|trans]] councillor for the city.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Johnson |first=James |date=2022-05-06 |title=Plymouth's first trans councillor says it is 'amazing' |url=https://www.plymouthherald.co.uk/news/plymouth-news/plymouths-first-trans-councillor-says-7044552 |access-date=2022-05-06 |website=PlymouthLive |language=en}}</ref>

== Aftermath ==

The council remained in no overall control. The Labour group leader and former council leader [[Tudor Evans]] said Labour had performed "better than anticipated" and that people "want the Tories gone".<ref name="Herald-results"/> Ian Poyser, elected as the city's first [[Green Party of England and Wales|Green Party]] councillor, said he wouldn't "any pacts or allegiances to either of those other two parties at this stage", referring to Labour and the Conservatives, saying he would try to enable "cross-party working in the background".<ref>{{Cite web |last1=Clark |first1=Daniel |last2=Churm |first2=Philip |date=2022-05-16 |title=Plymouth's first Green councillor rules out alliance |url=https://www.plymouthherald.co.uk/news/plymouth-news/plymouths-first-green-councillor-rules-7075866 |access-date=2022-05-17 |website=PlymouthLive |language=en}}</ref> The independent councillor George Wheeler, who had originally been elected as a Labour candidate, joined the Green Party later in May. Wheeler said he had left the Labour group, and later the Labour Party, because he "could no longer work with Plymouth's Labour leadership".<ref>{{Cite web |last=Eve |first=Carl |date=2022-05-16 |title=Independent Plymouth councillor says he has gone Green |url=https://www.plymouthherald.co.uk/news/plymouth-news/independent-plymouth-councillor-announces-gone-7086579 |access-date=2022-05-17 |website=PlymouthLive |language=en}}</ref> The ''Plymouth Herald'' reported that Bingley was planning to invite independent councillors who had left the Conservative group to rejoin.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Eve |first=Carl |date=2022-05-12 |title=City council leader inviting Independents into Tory fold |url=https://www.plymouthherald.co.uk/news/plymouth-news/plymouth-city-council-leader-set-7068425 |access-date=2022-05-17 |website=PlymouthLive |language=en}}</ref> One Conservative councillor, Dan Collins for Plympton Chaddlewood, and one former Conservative independent councillor, Shannon Burden, continued to serve as councillors despite having moved to [[Gloucestershire]].<ref>{{Cite web |last1=Eve |first1=Carl |last2=Churm |first2=Philip |date=2022-05-15 |title=Eight independents who hold the balance of power in Plymouth |url=https://www.plymouthherald.co.uk/news/plymouth-news/eight-independents-who-hold-balance-7069083 |access-date=2022-05-17 |website=PlymouthLive |language=en}}</ref> The independent councillors Lynda Bowyer, Shannon Burden, Nigel Churchill, Stephen Hulme and Kathy Watkin rejoined the Conservative group on 17 May, meaning that the Conservative Party held a majority of seats on the council.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Eve |first=Carl |date=2022-05-17 |title=Conservatives back in charge of Plymouth Council |url=https://www.plymouthherald.co.uk/news/plymouth-news/conservatives-back-charge-plymouth-city-7090254 |access-date=2022-05-17 |website=PlymouthLive |language=en}}</ref>
